subject: Request: temporary sticky-reservation / latency waiver for dedicated pool
messages:
From: Tina Long <tina.long@heliumgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool request + temporary latency waiver for launch testing

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’re ramping HeliumGrid’s chat summarization pilot and expect three short spikes per hour with heavy tail latency sensitivity during those spikes (p95/p99 matter). Our engineering lead asked whether Redwood can temporarily "stick" our reserved GPUs to the pool instances running our model so we avoid cold-KV-induced tail latency during the pilot.

Specifically we’re asking for:
- A one-week sticky-reservation window next week (2027-04-12 -> 2027-04-19) where a subset of the reserved nodes are pinned to our tenant to minimize preemption.
- A short-term latency waiver for 99th-percentile latency during that week, with a clear fallback plan (we still want automatic fallbacks to a compatible quantized variant if capacity is exceeded).
- Observability hooks (token-level latency and warm-cache hit rate metrics) during the window.

I attached our traffic pattern (traffic-profile-apr.csv). We’re flexible on the exact naming/implementation; goal is to avoid a single-day regression during pilot.

Can Redwood do this under an ad-hoc SLA? If so, we’ll need a brief writeup to run by procurement and our infra leads.

Thanks —
Tina
Tina Long
Product Engineering Manager, HeliumGrid

Attachment: traffic-profile-apr.csv (CSV, 34KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Long <tina.long@heliumgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool request + temporary latency waiver for launch testing

Hi Tina —

Appreciate the details and the pattern file — that helps a lot. Short answer: yes, we can support a short, scoped "sticky reservation" window and a temporary latency waiver with conditions. Outline below — if this aligns I’ll send a one-page SLA addendum and Ops playbook for signatures: 

Proposal (summary):
- Window: 2027-04-12 00:00 -> 2027-04-19 23:59 PT.
- Sticky reservation: reserve 4 nodes (your reserved pool) pinned to HeliumGrid for the window. These nodes will be warmed and excluded from standard preemption during the window except for catastrophic failures.
- Latency waiver: Redwood will not count p99 latency breaches against standard committed SLAs for the window, provided: 1) traffic matches the submitted profile (no >3x sudden scale-ups beyond attached CSV), and 2) HeliumGrid runs the agreed fallback variant if overall cluster saturation is hit.
- Fallback & safety: automatic routing to compatible quantized fallback model after queueing threshold X (we’ll propose X in the addendum).
- Observability: token-level latency + warm-cache hit-rate dashboard; alerting to your on-call and our on-call.
- Credits: if Redwood is the root cause of a platform-side failure (node loss, network partition), we’ll provide a proportional usage credit per our standard terms.

I attached a quick draft addendum (sla-proposal-sticky-reservation-draft.pdf). Ben and Marissa, PTAL at the operational bits (queue thresholds / preemption carveouts).

Next steps: confirm window and node count (4?), approve draft, sign addendum, schedule a brief canary deployment on 2027-04-11 (non-peak) to validate metrics.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-proposal-sticky-reservation-draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool request + temporary latency waiver for launch testing

Quick ops notes — lane for visibility and to flag tradeoffs.

Karthik / Marissa —
- Sticky reservation as described (node pinning) is doable but will reduce our flexible capacity by ~4 nodes for the window. That’s acceptable if we confirm no overlapping carveouts for other customers that week.
- Risk: pinned nodes reduce overall ability to absorb HW failures. To mitigate I recommend:
  1) Warm instance strategy: keep KV caches hot and pre-load typical prefixes before the window; we can run automated prefix-warms during off-hours.
  2) Canary run: single-node canary on 2027-04-11, validated metrics (p95/p99, cache-hit) before full stick.
  3) Queueing threshold: set soft-queue limit of 30 concurrent inflight requests per node; when exceeded, route to fallback model (quantized) and emit explicit SLO flag in dashboard.
- Monitoring/alerts: we need HeliumGrid to accept our standard alerting policy (pager threshold + email digests). Also need a named on-call (ops) contact in the addendum.

If HeliumGrid agrees to the canary + named on-call and the queueing threshold, I’ll greenlight the reservation in the control plane and lock the nodes for the window.

Ben
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

(Internal attachment: ops-runbook-sticky-reservation.md)

From: Tina Long <tina.long@heliumgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, HeliumGrid Ops <priority-ops@heliumgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool request + temporary latency waiver for launch testing

Karthik / Ben —

This looks good and reasonable. HeliumGrid accepts the window (2027-04-12 -> 2027-04-19) and the four-node pin. We agree to the canary on 2027-04-11 and to the queueing threshold + fallback routing described. Our on-call for the window will be: Priya Natarajan (priya.n@heliumgrid.com).

Please go ahead and send the one-page addendum + DocuSign link and we’ll route for internal procurement approval today. Also, please include the dashboard link and the alerting thresholds so our SREs can import them into our monitoring stack.

Thanks —
Tina

Attachment: none
